speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) what is the rationale for priority admission to co-located primary schools for students in MOE Kindergartens; and (b) what are the responses of parents and other preschools to this policy announcement.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) what is the number of Primary schools with MOE Kindergartens; (b) how many MOE Kindergartens will be located in the popular primary schools which have balloting in the last three years for Primary 1 registration; and (c) whether the priority admission for pupils of MOE Kindergartens that are co-located with the primary schools use the procedures and rules as the Primary 1 registration exercise.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) is committed to ensure that every child has a strong start and can access affordable and quality education.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We piloted the MOE Kindergartens (MKs) with this in mind, and the take-up rate and reception of parents have been positive.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In reviewing the pilot, MOE found that there are developmental benefits to young children when they remain in a familiar physical, social and educational environment.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In addition, we have received feedback from parents who said that they hoped that the number of "transitions" can be reduced.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As MKs cater to Kindergarten 1 (K1) and Kindergarten 2 (K2) children, MK children typically transit twice in their early childhood: first, from nursery to MK; and second, from MK to the primary school.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: From the MK pilot experience, school-based MKs have greater synergies with primary schools which, in turn, better support the children's transition from K2 to Primary 1.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: All the new MKs will be located within primary schools.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The new MKs will generally be located in estates where there is a higher demand for preschool places and the schools they will be located within are likely to be Government schools.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is too early to say if these schools will ballot in which phase of future Primary 1 Registration Exercises, or whether, indeed, they will face balloting at all.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Regardless, MOE ensures that there are sufficient school places on a regional basis so that no child will have to travel long distances to his or her primary school.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Many parents have welcomed MOE's plan to expand the number of MKs, as well as the introduction of the Phase 2A2 admission eligibility.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: At the same time, some parents have expressed concerns that the admissions eligibility for MK children may bring the stress of primary school admission upstream to the kindergarten years.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The planned K1 intake for the MKs will be significantly below that of the planned Primary 1 intake of the primary school that the MK is located within, so that there will be sufficient access for children who are not from the MK at the Primary 1 Registration Exercise.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In addition, at least a minimum of 40 places will always be reserved for Phases 2B and 2C at every primary school, to ensure open access to the school.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Nevertheless, at 50 MKs, MKs will only make up about 20% of the preschool landscape, which means that parents will still have sufficient choice and good preschools that are able to provide quality services that meet the needs and preferences of families will continue to play an important role in this sector.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When selecting a preschool for their children, parents consider factors, such as the quality of the programmes and teachers, location and the service model.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For example, some parents may prefer their children to be in the same child care centre from their infant years all the way till K2.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Hence, we hope that all preschool operators will continue to invest in uplifting quality and to evolve their services to cater to the different needs and preferences of parents.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The introduction of Phase 2A2 admission eligibility for MK children is a pilot scheme.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: MOE will continually monitor demand and the needs of parents, take in feedback and assess how well the admission eligibility is working in achieving the outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It will be sometime before we will have 50 MKs and we hope to draw on the experience of operating these MKs to do proper refining and review.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If necessary, we will always do these refinements as part of our continuing journey to improve the education system.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: MOE has initially entered this space with these MKs as a pilot to uplift the quality and raise the bar of preschool education in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: If so, how does it intend to level the playing field, especially for the preferred operators it has appointed, with MOE having a structural advantage, for example, in being able to implement policies of priority admission of children into co-located primary schools.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I would like to ask what the vision is.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, we are finished very much with the initial piloting of the 15 MKs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The areas where we have developed appropriate teaching or learning resources, we have started to share with the general early childhood sector.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Since 2016, we have made available some of the resources that we have found to be very useful in the children's learning.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When we come to the teaching of languages, we use big books to tell stories to the children to captivate their interest and facilitate their learning both in English and the Mother Tongues.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We have also put into the Nurturing Early Learners Portal some of the best practices in the MKs to make them available online for the early childhood educators' community.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Furthermore, MOE participates in various conferences that are organised by the Early Childhood Development Agency or other agencies to share the best practices in early childhood education.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For the question on a level playing field, MK and the Early Years Centre collaboration is a pilot scheme.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, we have finished with the MK pilot, but now we are looking into providing an added option for parents, where they may be looking for a MK education for their children.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, we are looking to partner with some Anchor Operator Preschools (AOPs) to develop this partnering of childcare services from the early years.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It may be two to four years old at the AOP childcare, and then to MK.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This is an added option in the market.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, there is ample space for different operators to participate in this very important pre-school education sector.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But more importantly, from MOE's perspective, the level playing field is for the child.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: That is why, in all the different programmes that we put forward, as I have mentioned earlier, we ensure that it is affordable and easily accessible for children from lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This promotes better social mobility and social mixing in our schools and this is very much the central objective in why we set up MKs as well.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I just need a clarification or assurance from the Minister that every MK child will be able to secure a place where the MK is located in.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is too early to give such guarantees and probably impossible to give such guarantees.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But what I can say is that, in the framing of the whole scheme, we have ensured that the number of places in Primary 1 is significantly more than the MK.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: From data, we also see that parents do exercise choices other than progressing their children from the MK to the primary school.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, with a combination of such factors, we think that the likelihood of an MK child progressing through Primary 1 of the same locality will be quite high, but I do not think that I can give a guarantee at this stage.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Are there primary schools that are co-located with MKs that have become more popular because of MKs?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The second question is: what is the timeframe to realise the 50 MKs in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: My third supplementary question is: if one or a few MKs become so popular that the demand outstrips the supply, then what will be the admission criteria for such popular MKs?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Could the Member please repeat the earlier two questions?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The first question is: are there primary schools with MKs that have become more popular because of MKs?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: If such primary schools become more popular because of MK, it is a good impact.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The second question is: what is the timeframe to realise the 50 MKs?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: MOE is increasing the number from 15 to 50, right?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: So, what is the timeframe to do so?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The third question is: when certain MKs become so popular where the demand outstrips supply, then what will be the admission criteria for such popular MKs?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We do not have the data because we just introduced the MK concept only a few years ago, and we did not monitor whether the primary schools have become more popular because of the MKs.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: There is a variety of factors, so I do not have the definitive answer to the first question.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: On the last question, there is already an MK admission framework that is published on the MOE website.
